# Unreleased

Staging note for the next release. Fold it into that release's `<tag>.md` (the release job reads `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md`) and delete this file.

## New

- **Test connection checks the model id.** For Anthropic and OpenAI (and OpenAI-compatible servers that have a models list), Test connection, in the add-model form and `continuous test-connection --model`, asks the provider about the configured id with `GET /v1/models/{id}`. An id the key cannot reach is named with close matches from the list ("Did you mean claude-opus-5-5?"); Anthropic's answer adds the context window, maximum output, image and PDF input, thinking types and deprecation dates, and OpenAI's adds a shutdown date. A refused key, a rate limit, a network failure and an endpoint without a models API are told apart and reported as "not checked"; none of them fails the connection or a chat request.

- **Costs say where their prices came from and as of when.** The console's Total Usage, the terminal agent's `/info` and its end-of-run summary (`--verbose`) add a line such as "Prices: Anthropic list prices, as of 2026-11-02", "Prices: OpenRouter model list, fetched 3 h ago", "Prices: your config" or "Prices: community catalogue (models.dev), 2026-11-10 — estimate", and the served-tier note when a provider served a request at a non-standard tier. `-p --format stream-json` adds `priceSource` (and `servedTier`) to each `usage` line and `priceSources` (and `servedTiers`) to the `result` line; these are optional fields, so the schema version stays 1.

- **Bedrock: a 0 quota is named before the first request.** If your AWS credentials may read Service Quotas (`servicequotas:ListServiceQuotas`, optional), Test connection and selecting a Bedrock model warn when the account's tokens-per-minute (or requests-per-minute) quota for that model is 0 in the region, with a link to the Service Quotas console: "<model> has a 0 tokens-per-minute quota in <region> for this account; request an increase in Service Quotas". Without the permission, Test connection still succeeds and shows one quiet line, "Quota check skipped: this profile lacks servicequotas:ListServiceQuotas"; that answer is remembered per profile and region for a day (or until the credentials change). Throttling, network errors, a region without Service Quotas and slow answers (5 seconds) are skipped quietly; nothing waits for the check. A Bedrock API key cannot read Service Quotas, so the check is skipped for it.
- **Bedrock prices from the AWS Price List.** Cost estimates for Bedrock models use the AWS Price List for the selected model's region, ahead of the built-in prices, and name it with its date. Flex and priority requests are priced at their own rates where AWS lists them. The file is public (no credentials, no IAM) and is downloaded from `pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` only when a Bedrock model is configured, under **Model information updates** (Automatic: on selecting a Bedrock model and once per refresh interval; Only when I ask: on Bedrock Test connection; Off: never). Firewall allowlists: expect `pricing.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` and `servicequotas.<region>.amazonaws.com` (TCP 443) on machines with a Bedrock model.

- **See what fills the context window.** Beside the session cost under the prompt, a context meter shows the share of the model's window in use ("Context 43%"), in the theme's warning colour from 60 percent and its error colour from 80 percent or once the oldest messages are being left out. Click it, press Enter on it, or rest the pointer on it to see what the context holds: a bar and a table of the system prompt, tool definitions, rules, attached files, your messages, replies, tool calls, tool results, terminal output, images, reasoning, free space and the room kept for the reply, with the largest items by name ("Read src/app.ts: 12k") and the prompt cache state. The split is estimated and scaled to the provider's token count. Compact now and New session are in the same panel. It replaces the small battery that appeared from 60 percent with these actions in a hover tooltip. Nothing about what is sent to the model changes.

## Behaviour changes

- **The selected Anthropic or OpenAI chat model's details are refreshed from its own provider**, with Model information updates on **Automatic** (the default). A few seconds after you select the model, then once per refresh interval (24 hours by default), Continuous sends one `GET /v1/models/{id}` to the API base configured for that model, with your key and `requestOptions`. No other host is contacted, only the selected model is asked about, and nothing waits for the answer. The answer is kept in `model-catalog/provider-<provider>-<hash>.json` (the hash covers the API base and key; the key is not written) and supplies the context window and default maximum output where your config does not set them, ahead of the bundled model data; Anthropic's built-in default of 8192 output tokens is never raised by it. A deprecation, retirement or shutdown date shows as the warning chip beside the model picker (now for OpenAI models too). A refused key or a failure leaves the bundled data in use and retries later; an endpoint without a models API is not asked again in that session. **Only when I ask** limits this to Test connection; **Off** sends nothing and ignores kept answers.

- **A last-resort price from the community catalogue, models.dev.** When a selected model has no price from a price you entered, a provider list or the curated tables, Continuous can price it from [models.dev](https://models.dev) (community-maintained, MIT), labelled "community catalogue (models.dev), <date> — estimate". It never replaces a better source, and `--max-budget-usd` is refused on it unless `--budget-allow-unpriced` is given (the cap is then held on the estimate); the Auto reviewer's shadow budget is never held on it.
  - **New egress, `models.dev` (TCP 443)**: one `GET https://models.dev/api.json`, no key, body or model name, headers `accept` and `user-agent: continuous` only. Only while a selected model (the IDE's chat or reviewer model, the terminal agent's model) is unpriced, and never when model information updates are off. With Automatic (the default) it is checked 15 to 60 seconds after the IDE starts and 1 to 3 seconds after the terminal agent starts, then at least every 6 hours, and fetched when the copy is missing or older than the refresh interval (24 hours); with Only when I ask, only on Refresh now in the IDE. The trimmed copy (prices only, at most 4 MB) is `model-catalog/models-dev.json`. PRIVACY.md and the egress allowlist (class D) list it.

## Fixes

- Bedrock errors now name the cause when a model is refused for quota or account reasons. "Not available for this account" (what Bedrock answers when the account's tokens-per-minute quota for the model is 0, even with model access granted) points at Service Quotas instead of the model access page; "your account is currently being verified" (the first use of a region) says to wait; a throttled request says the quota is used up and that throttling on the very first request can mean a quota of 0.
- Costs now carry where their prices came from and as of when (Anthropic list prices, OpenAI pricing page, AWS Price List, the downloaded OpenRouter list, or a price you entered), for the cost displays to show. When Bedrock or Anthropic report that a request was served at a non-standard tier (flex, priority, batch), the cost breakdown says the figure is the standard-tier price and whether the actual charge is lower or higher.
- Adding Anthropic models reads image support and the scheduled retirement date from Anthropic's model list, and the Bedrock model list keeps image support and the legacy, extended-access and end-of-life dates Bedrock reports.
